findings.value: A museum in Bow, E3, in a converted warehouse where Dr Barnardo's ragged school taught poor children, with a Victorian-style classroom where pupils take lessons.

evidence.quote: One hundred and fifty years ago, Dr Barnardo opened the first of his
teaching literacy and basic arithmetic to poor children in a converted warehouse
the Ragged School Museum in Copperfield Rd, Bow, next to the canal
In 1990, the building became a museum of the life and works of Dr Barnardo, with a classroom where pupils from schools around London come to experience nineteenth century disciplinarian education.
At the heart of the Ragged School Museum is our unique classroom, where each year some 16,000 children come to experience a glimpse of Victorian life.

findings.value: The museum says some 16,000 children a year come to its classroom, and Spitalfields Life describes pupils from schools around London visiting.
